subject: Critical Thinking
title: Building a Personal Fact-Checking Routine
description: A quick win: understand Building a Personal Fact-Checking Routine.

hook.text: A journalist shares a breaking news story. Within minutes, three different 'fact-checks' contradict each other.

buildup.text: Professional fact-checkers use systematic methods. Amateurs usually just Google and pick the result they like.

discovery.text: The SIFT method: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace claims to their origin.

twist.text: Most misinformation spreads in the first minutes. A 30-second SIFT check before sharing blocks most of it.

climax.text: Lateral reading — checking what others say about a source rather than reading it deeply — beats deep analysis.

punchline.text: The best fact-check is the one you do before sharing.

quiz.question: What does SIFT stand for in fact-checking?
options: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace claims

details.summary: A personal fact-checking routine is a set of habitual practices you apply before accepting or sharing information. Building this routine transforms occasional skepticism into a consistent thinking habit that operates automatically.
details.whyItMatters: Sporadic fact-checking is like sporadic exercise — it helps in the moment but does not build lasting resilience. Habitual fact-checking becomes an automatic defense.
takeaways: Consistent routines outperform occasional effort for critical thinking
Automate key checks: source, evidence, alternatives, conflicts of interest
The goal is habit formation, not perfection on any single check

faq.question: What should a minimal daily fact-checking routine include?
faq.answer: Before sharing: check the source. Before reacting emotionally: pause and verify the claim. Once daily: read one article from a source you normally avoid. Weekly: reflect on a belief you hold and look for disconfirming evidence. These habits compound over time.

faq.question: How long does it take to develop a reliable fact-checking habit?
faq.answer: Research on habit formation suggests 60 to 90 days of consistent practice. Start with the simplest check — pausing before sharing — and add layers as each becomes automatic. Linking the habit to an existing routine like morning news reading increases consistency.
